newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: African leaders to attend Bangui peace signing.
newsitem.headline: African leaders to attend Bangui peace signing.

text.p: Four African heads of state will travel to the Central African Republic by January 23 for the signing of a peace deal to end its third army mutiny in under a year, the chief mediator said on Saturday.
Malian general Amadou Toumani Toure told politicians he would leave to brief the presidents of Chad, Gabon, Burkina Faso and Mali once the deal had been drafted.
"The end of the conciliation and dialogue will take place in the presence of the heads of state of the international committee before January 23," he said.
Mutinies in April and May began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust Ange-Felix Patasse, a northern civilian politician who won presidential elections in 1993.
A truce between mutineers, mainly minority Yakomas from the south, and army loyalists, expires on January 23.

The four presidents -- Omar Bongo of Gabon, Alpha Oumar Konare of Mali, Blaise Compaore of Burkina Faso and Idriss Deby of Chad -- visited Bangui and launched the mediation bid at the request of a Franco-African summit in Burkina Faso in December.
Committees have made recommendations on security, social and political issues and on reconciliation and restitution.

French troops, in the former French colony under a defence pact, patrol the capital and form a buffer between mutineers and their foes in the presidential guard. Mediators have suggested African peacekeepers take over, an idea France has welcomed.
The latest mutiny, which began on November 15, degenerated into ethnic feuding. The overall death toll runs into hundreds.
